title: RC-MemStop: Risk-Controlled Early Stopping for Long-Context Memory Agents

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is "provides training-free early stopping for memory agents with explicit safety guarantees on broken-success risk." No prior paper explicitly addresses early stopping for memory agents with safety guarantees on broken-success risk. Papers like [18] (Confidence-Guided Early Stopping) and [17] (SAFE-KD) discuss early stopping mechanisms, but they focus on adaptive halting or distillation frameworks without explicit guarantees on broken-success risk. Similarly, [27] (Game-Theoretic Statistics and Safe Anytime-Valid Inference) and [14] (Safe Logrank Test) discuss error control under continuous monitoring but do not target memory agents or broken-success risk. Thus, no prior paper shares the same purpose.

### Mechanism
The mechanism, "RC-MemStop applies conformal risk control with an answer-stability stopping rule (terminate after k consecutive matching draft answers) and the Waudby-Smith-Ramdas betting bound to select the least conservative k satisfying a user-specified risk budget epsilon," is partially covered. Papers [5] (Conformal Risk Control) and [13] (STaR-Bets) both discuss betting bounds and conformal risk control, but neither applies these techniques to answer-stability stopping rules or memory agents. Paper [18] (Confidence-Guided Early Stopping) uses Bayesian posterior mass for adaptive halting, which is conceptually similar to stability-based stopping but does not employ conformal risk control or betting bounds. Paper [17] (SAFE-KD) applies conformal risk control to early-exit networks, but its mechanism focuses on hierarchical distillation rather than answer-stability stopping. Thus, the mechanism is partially covered but not substantively equivalent.

### Evaluation
The evaluation facet is "first application of conformal risk control to memory agent early stopping; UCB-calibrated thresholds maintain user-specified risk budgets with zero violations across all 8 configurations on MemAgent with 448K-896K token contexts." Papers [5] (Conformal Risk Control), [13] (STaR-Bets), and [18] (Confidence-Guided Early Stopping) all use conformal risk control or betting bounds in their evaluation setups, but none applies these methods to memory agents or long-context inference. However, the evaluation design itself — conformal risk control with calibrated thresholds — is not novel, as it appears in [5] and [13]. The specific application to memory agents belongs to the domain facet, not evaluation. Thus, the evaluation is covered.

### Domain
The domain is "long-context LLM memory agents / efficient inference." Papers [3] (Conformal Thinking: Risk Control for Reasoning on a Compute Budget) and [21] (A Survey of LLM Reasoning in Healthcare and Medicine) both address reasoning and inference in LLMs, including compute-efficient methods. Paper [18] (Confidence-Guided Early Stopping) also discusses efficient inference in LLMs. While none of these papers specifically targets memory agents with long contexts, they operate in the same general application area of LLM reasoning and efficient inference. Thus, the domain is covered.
